extracted.intended_audience: Flipboard users — individual curators, creators, publishers, and community-builders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and maintaining Flipboard magazines and feeds across four curation goals: building expertise, building community, personal archiving, and distributing your own content. Advice covers frequency, source selection, metadata, platform features, and engagement tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency & activity
rubrics_metrics.description: “Consistency is everything. It’s an investment—just like Twitter or LinkedIn—and you should be going for gold... It’s important to stay active on Flipboard if you’re curating for an audience or desire credibility. The world moves fast—and your followers are depending on you for their info fix. So curate daily...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be regularly present and persistent (daily if possible) to maintain credibility and keep followers engaged; inactivity undermines authority and usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showcase domain expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: “You’re growing your personal brand and your footprint in a profession. You want others to know that you’re an authority in this space, and your curation is going to prove it... go for gold in terms of showcasing your domain knowledge, speed, and passion.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flip major news, trends, and cool finds in your field to demonstrate knowledge, quickness in surfacing important items, and genuine enthusiasm; prior track record helps credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source mix / plurality
rubrics_metrics.description: “Include authoritative sources and expert voices, but also surprise and delight with lesser-known publishers, people, and content of all media types... look for stories that *really* matter from a plurality of sources.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance trusted/authoritative sources with unexpected or niche finds; draw from multiple sources to give a well-rounded view and avoid echo chambers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add original commentary / curatorial voice
rubrics_metrics.description: “Use the pencil icon to add your own commentary to your picks and to highlight important quotes. It’ll demonstrate that you not only carefully read what you’re recommending, but also that you have a unique perspective to share.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate picks with your perspective or highlights to show curation judgment; commentary signals you've engaged with the item and helps differentiate your magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a clear point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: “Have a point of view that makes you an indispensable voice in the conversation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curate with a consistent editorial stance or theme so followers understand what to expect and why your collection is valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum collection size before public promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: “When you have at least 10 items*, share your magazine via networks like LinkedIn and encourage people to follow you on Flipboard... (*Yes, a random number. The point is to have enough content to give people a well-rounded idea of your approach.)”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build a small but substantive body of work (≈10 items suggested) before promoting externally so visitors can quickly assess your curation style and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the community
rubrics_metrics.description: “Comment on and like stories in other people’s magazines, invite members of your community to curate with you, and/or send stories to others with a thoughtful note like ‘You might like this’ or ‘This would be perfect in your magazine.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively interact (likes, comments, re-flips, direct shares) to build relationships and visibility; engagement signals genuine interest and helps grow your audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be hyper-aware of audience expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: “‘Good curation’ here is hyper-aware of what the tribe would expect to see, what they need to know, and what you want them to know. Your finger is on the pulse.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the interests, norms, and informational needs of your target community and select items accordingly to remain relevant and authoritative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite collaboration / use collaborative magazines
rubrics_metrics.description: “Ask a fellow passionista to share stories together... Here’s how to set up a collaborative magazine. (It’s really fun.)”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Flipboard’s collaborative magazines to co-curate, increase content diversity, and engage contributors from your community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize collections for personal use
rubrics_metrics.description: “This collection needs to serve only one master: you... create a magazine for each interest, project, or goal. Think of these as a kind of filing system.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When curating for personal reference, prioritize organization and retrieval: use distinct magazines per topic/project and sensible naming to find items later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalize feed by following topics and creators
rubrics_metrics.description: “Personalize your Flipboard by following the topics, people and publications that map to your ambitions. Your ‘home feed’ (aka ‘For You’) will always contain a cross‑section of the best and newest stuff being shared across your interests.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specific topics, people, and publications to tailor what Flipboard surfaces to you and make saving/curating more efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazines can be public or private
rubrics_metrics.description: “Flip stories you want to save in thematic magazines for access later. Magazines can be public or private.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose visibility per magazine depending on whether the collection is for personal use, community sharing, or public distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include varied media types
rubrics_metrics.description: “Flip stories relevant to your expertise in a magazine. You can flip articles, photos, videos, and audio from nearly anywhere.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mix articles, images, videos, and audio to create richer, multi-format collections that appeal to different consumption preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content quality & audience resonance for owned content
rubrics_metrics.description: “What’s ‘good’ in this case depends on the quality of the content itself, what will resonate with your target audience, and how well the stories render on Flipboard.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When distributing your own content, prioritize high-quality, audience-relevant material and ensure it displays well on the platform to maximize impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize RSS / rendering for platform
rubrics_metrics.description: “This is how to set up your RSS feed for optimal viewing on our platform.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure RSS and article metadata so stories render properly on Flipboard (follow linked guidance) to improve reader experience and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flip into magazines to gain platform priority
rubrics_metrics.description: “Flipping content into magazines is one of the ways for those items to get priority in our system. You can flip posts manually or apply to be a publisher…”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manually flipping items into magazines can increase visibility; use platform features to surface your content more prominently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply to be a publisher / auto-publish via RSS
rubrics_metrics.description: “Apply to be a publisher, which allows you automatically publish from RSS to Flipboard. (Please note: the wait time for this feature is currently between one and two months in the U.S. and longer for other countries.)”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider publisher status for automated distribution from your RSS feed; plan for application wait times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear, relevant metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: “Make sure any content you create has clear, relevant metadata (title, tags, keywords) so that our system knows which topics to sort stories into.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accurate titles, descriptive tags, and keywords to help Flipboard classify your content into appropriate topics and reach interested audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage engagement to trigger algorithmic distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: “Our algorithm favors items with strong engagement, so encouraging your followers to read, like and share what you’re curating tells our system to pay attention to those stories and consider them for further distribution on Flipboard.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt readers to engage (read, like, share) to increase the chances of algorithmic amplification and wider distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote magazines externally
rubrics_metrics.description: “When you have at least 10 items, share your magazine via networks like LinkedIn and encourage people to follow you on Flipboard to get alerts about future additions.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-promote your Flipboard magazines on other social networks to attract followers who will engage and grow your audience.
